statement: The hour hand of a clock points exactly halfway between the 10 and the 11. Where does the minute hand point?

choices.misconception: I thought halfway between two numbers meant a quarter of the hour had gone, so I put the minute hand on 3.
I thought the minute hand points at the number the hour hand has just passed, so I chose 10.
I thought the minute hand points at the number the hour hand is moving towards, so I chose 11.
I thought the minute hand is on 12 whenever the hour hand is near a number, as it is at an o'clock time.

hints: How far through the hour has the hour hand gone?
The hour hand moves from one number to the next in exactly one hour. Work out what fraction of that hour has passed, then find where the minute hand is after that fraction of a turn.
Halfway from 10 to 11 means half of the hour after 10 o'clock has passed, so the time is half past 10. After half an hour the minute hand has made half a turn from 12.

solutions.reliable: The hour hand takes one hour to move from the 10 to the 11. Halfway there means half an hour has passed since 10 o'clock, so the time is 10:30. In half an hour the minute hand turns half way round the clock, from 12 to 6. The transferable idea: the hour hand's position between two numbers tells you the fraction of the hour that has passed.
solutions.elegant: Picture 10:30 on any clock: the minute hand points straight down at 6 and the hour hand sits halfway between 10 and 11. Reading the clock backwards from the hour hand gives the same picture.

whyOnTest: It checks that the hour hand creeps between numbers in step with the minute hand, which students who only read o'clock times miss.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
